Getting started

Start here

The app runs in your phone browser and keeps working without a signal. Records stay on the phone until you sign in; then they follow your account to every phone you use.

How to

  1. Open the app address in Chrome or Safari.
  2. Add it to the home screen: Share › Add to Home Screen on iPhone, or the ⋮ menu › Add to home screen on Android. It then opens like an app.
  3. Start on Home: each tile opens one part of the app. The menu across the top has the main pages; some have a second row.
  4. Tap the ? beside the page name on any page to come back to the right part of this guide.
  • Nothing is lost when the signal drops: entries made offline wait on the phone and go out when it is back online.

Open Start here in Roast ›

Sign in and sync

One account per farm or business. Sign in on every phone that should see the same records.

How to

  1. Open the account page (the round person button at the top right).
  2. Type your email and tap Send code. Type the code from the email.
  3. Records already on the phone are sent to your account, and records from your other phones come in.
  4. To have staff enter records for you, sign in on their phone with the same account.
  • "Waiting to send" beside an entry means the phone has not been online since; it goes on its own.
  • Sign out on a phone you no longer use.

Farm

Your estate and plots, and what happens on the land: soil, flowering, rows, map, weather, field work.

Estates and plots
Each plot keeps its variety, plant age, spacing and shade.Planting density is worked out from spacing. Plots link to harvests, processing runs and green lots, so every bag traces back to where it grew. Each estate keeps the producer address and contact buyers ask for.
Soil and soil life
Soil type, care practices, soil tests and inputs for each plot.A checklist of four soil principles (moving resources, living roots, undisturbed patches, diversity), soil test results rated against Indian Soil Health Card bands, an inputs log, and a summary of what studies found about soil and the cup.
Plot and cup
Cup scores for coffee from each plot, side by side with your other plots.Gathers green-lot scores and Cup sessions of roasts made from that plot. Over seasons it shows which plots and practices give better cups.
Flowering timing
From the blossom shower date: when backing is due and when fruit drop peaks.Backing shower 15 to 20 days after blossom; normal fruit drop peaks 90 to 120 days after flowering (CCRI).
Coffee varieties and words
Arabica and Robusta varieties of India and the world, plus coffee terms.Variety, varietal, clone, selection and other words explained. Sources from TNAU, Counter Culture, World Coffee Research and others.
Map
Mark plots, stores, drying yards, houses and spots on a satellite map.Area, boundary, side lengths, distances and terrain heights. Colours by kind, layers, tidy names. Share as Google Maps links, KML, GeoJSON or a printed sheet. Green lots show where they grew.
Trails
Walk a farm or a buyer visit and record the path, with stops, notes and photos.Like a hiking trail app, for coffee. Distance, time and climb. Kept only on your device, never in the cloud. Save a trail pack (zip with photos and a page that opens anywhere), GPX for hiking apps, KML for Google Earth or GeoJSON, and open them again later.
Rows and plants
Each row of a plot on the map, with every plant numbered at the spacing you give.Draw a row, walk it with the phone, take rows from a trail walked up and down them, or copy one row across the plot. Labels like R3-12, status and notes for each plant, CSV and GeoJSON.

How to grow and pick.

Lots

From harvest to green coffee: picking, processing, green lots, passports and EUDR, linked from plant to bag.

Harvest log
Each day's picking: plots, baskets, ripeness, floaters and Brix.Total cherry adds up from baskets. Average Brix and range from your readings.
  1. Open Origin › Harvest and tap New.
  2. Give the date, the plots picked and the picking (selective, strip, gleaning or mixed).
  3. Under Weights, add a basket row for each basket or picker, with its kg in the kg box; the total cherry adds up.
  4. Optional: ripe, under-ripe, over-ripe and floater %, and Brix readings.
  5. Save. The harvest gets its code and links to its plots.
Processing runs
Step by step: sorting, pulping, fermentation, washing, drying, resting, hulling, grading.Each step keeps times, weights and readings (temperature, pH, Brix, moisture, water activity, air humidity) with small charts and guide ranges from credited sources. Running timers, yields and outturn are worked out.
  1. Open Origin › Process and tap New.
  2. Pick the pathway and the source harvests (or type the cherry in, if it came from elsewhere).
  3. Add the steps as they happen: floating and sorting, pulping, fermentation, drying, with times and readings.
  4. Save. The run links back to its harvests and on to the green lot it makes.
Inoculation (yeasts and bacteria)
Product, dose, rehydration and timing for fermentation with selected yeasts.Suggested dose for your cherry weight, rehydration water, temperature and time checks, typical durations by process and cost per kg. Figures from Lallemand's published sheets.
Rehydration calculator
Water to add to over-dried green coffee to reach a target moisture.Enter starting moisture, target and batch size.
Green lots
Moisture, water activity, density, screen size, grade and stock left.Water activity can be estimated from moisture. Stock left goes down as roasts use the lot. Lineage shows the process, harvests and plots behind it. The EUDR section holds the product form, HS code and the importer's statement reference, and names any plot data still missing.
  1. Open Origin › Green lots and tap New.
  2. Choose the process it came from, or, for bought coffee, fill in the origin as the seller states it (farm, producer, region, country, variety, process).
  3. Add moisture, grade and kg; the lot keeps its stock as roasts, samples and sales draw from it.
  4. Open the lot to reach its passport, EUDR lot file, sack labels and the For a buyer sheet.
Plot and lot homes
A plot or green lot opens as its home: a short summary, chips to its sections, and the chain it sits in.A plot shows variety, area, last harvest and its land check, with chips for Location, Land check, Plants, Soil, Flowering, Plot and cup, Map, Rows and Photos, and what came from it (harvests, runs, green lots). A green lot shows where it came from (plot, harvest, run) and its roasts, kg left and moisture, with chips for the lot, quality, EUDR and labels. Harvests, process runs and roasts show the same chain. Each link says how it is known: Direct when the two records name each other, Derived when worked out through another record. For a buyer gathers the passport link, the EUDR lot file, the EU plot file (exact outline, so share it only with the buyer who needs it) and sack labels.
EUDR: selling into Europe
What the EU deforestation rule asks of growers, and where each piece lives in the app.Product form, HS code, statement reference and a plot data hint on each green lot. Producer address and contact on each estate, with the grower registration from Land and dues. Guidance, not legal advice.
Lot passports and QR
Signed, linked records for each lot from farm to roast, with a QR for the bag and handoffs to buyers.Open a green lot in Origin and tap Passport and QR. Each step is signed on the phone that recorded it and linked to the one before; each day's entries are stamped into the Bitcoin public record through OpenTimestamps. Send the lot to a buyer by email; they confirm the weight and add their roasts. Anyone scanning the QR sees every check run in their own browser, a weight check, and files to verify the stamp independently. Farm location is shown only if you choose.
Legality pack
Producer, land papers, licences, taxes and team on one page for a buyer.Gathered from Origin, Land and dues and Team and wages, with gaps shown. Wages and names stay private: it says only how many people are on record. Print it or save it as a PDF. It lists what is recorded; it is not a certificate.

Roast and cup

Roasting, colour, brewing, cupping and water.

New roast
Set up the coffee and green lot, then open the timer.Pick the green lot so its stock and lineage follow the roast.
  1. Tap Start New Roast (or Quick Roast for no setup).
  2. Fill in what you know: roast number, coffee code, estate, bean or lot, green weight, moisture, machine, charge temperature, target.
  3. Tap Save & Roast: the Roast timer opens with these details filled in.
Roast timer
Log temperatures and events as you roast: charge, turning, bottom, first crack, drop.Rate of rise, development time and DTR as you go, with an optional DTR drop guide.
  1. Choose what you read: ET + BT, BT only or ET only, and °C or °F.
  2. Tap Start at charge.
  3. At each interval tap Enter BT (and Enter ET) and type the reading; the curve and rate of rise draw as you go.
  4. Tap the events as they happen: Turning, Yellow, Maillard, First Crack, Second Crack, Drop.
  5. Tap Finish, add roasted weight and colour, then Save on device. Open Roastbook to see it.
Roast graph
The curve, rate of rise and phases of a roast.Total time, development, DTR and weight loss. Print or save as PDF, or export CSV.
Roastbook
All your finished roasts: search, filter, compare.Compare curves side by side. Export a roast to CSV, Artisan (.alog) or Artisan JSON / Cropster.
  1. Open Roastbook: every finished roast, newest first.
  2. Search or filter to find a roast; open it to see its curve, phases, weight loss and chain back to the green lot.
  3. Compare with other roasts to lay curves side by side.
  4. From a roast: + Brew or + Cupping, download it (CSV, Artisan .alog, Artisan JSON / Cropster), or Save to cloud.
Colour check
Record roast colour for any coffee: your roasts, bought coffee or samples. With only a phone photo, get a ballpark roast level and Agtron.A phone photo or a meter's L*a*b* alone gives a ballpark: roast name, Agtron Gourmet and Commercial, SCA tile, Tonino and Colorette, with a confidence level that tightens as you add meter readings. Type every number your meter screen shows (Agtron, Colorette, ColorTrack, roast name) and KoffyKraft learns its scales. Shows where the roast sits between first and second crack on the UC Davis colour curve. Meters: Agtron Gourmet and Commercial, Lighttells, Javalytics, Tonino, SCA tiles, and ColorTrack, Colorette or Neotec learned from your own paired readings. Shows each reading on the other scales, and colour values as CIELAB, LCh, Hunter Lab, XYZ and sRGB or HEX. Or measure from a phone photo with a white card. Names the roast level on three charts, tracks the ground to whole-bean gap, ΔE against a reference and nearest matches. Saved like brews, with cloud sync.
Capture and OCR
Photograph a label or note and turn it into text on your phone.Text recognition runs on the device; you confirm values before they are saved.
Brew log
Each brew with recipe, grind, water, rest days, TDS and extraction.Brew timers for one or several brews at once, with cut-off alarms.
  1. Open Cup and tap + Brew (Log brew in the Guided view).
  2. Pick the roast or coffee, the method and brewer, and fill in dose, water, water °C, grinder and grind setting, bloom and time.
  3. Taste and add flavour notes (Pick flavour notes) and a score.
  4. Save. Repeat last copies the recipe for the next brew; a Bluetooth scale can fill the coffee and water weights.
Dial-in pathways
From your brew to a target: sweeter, brighter, fuller, less bitter, cleaner, steadier.Exact water and dose to hit a strength and extraction, a brew control chart, roast-aware advice and "what stands out in the cup" causes. Studies credited, no guarantees.
Cupping
SCA, Barista Hustle style, Robusta (CQI) and simple forms.Guided or full views, flavour notes picker, off-flavour finder, scores per sample.
  1. Open Cup and tap + Cupping.
  2. Add each sample (+ Add sample), from your roasts or bought coffee, and the water per bowl.
  3. Score each sample: fragrance and aroma, flavour, aftertaste, acidity, body, balance, sweetness, clean cups, overall.
  4. Add tasters with + Taster if more than one person cups. Save; scores show on the roast and its green lot.
Tasting tests
Triangle, describe the difference, preference, and palate training.Blind codes, statistics for triangle and preference tests, and sour, sweet and salt ranking with ingredients to buy.
Brew guide
How brewers work.
How to brew, step by step
Numbered steps for every brewer in the guide: pour-over cones, immersion brewers, siphon, espresso and lever, moka, South Indian filter, phin, Turkish, Napoletana, cold brew, cold drip and nitro.What you need, each step with its time, what to watch for and how to care for the brewer, at three levels, from the makers' own instructions where they exist. Brew with steps runs a timer that buzzes at each step.
Brewing protocols
Repeatable ways of working: a standard cup, measuring strength, dial-in, freshness and freezing, cold brew, tasting roast changes.Built from the SCA Gold Cup figures and studies on freshness (ZHAW), cold brew (Cordoba 2019) and roast development (Alstrup 2020, Gloess 2014).
Water
Mix hot and cold water to a set temperature, and make brewing water from two concentrates.Weight or volume, vessel loss, and published recipes.

In every KoffyKraft app

Estates and plots

Each estate and its plots, with area, GPS point and the details that matter for the crop. Every other page picks from this list.

How to

  1. Add the estate first: name, area, GPS point (tap 📍 standing there).
  2. Add each plot under it. Fields marked * are needed.
  3. Mark the outline on the Map for an exact area and for buyers who ask where the crop grew.
  • In drop-downs each estate shows first as "Whole …", then its plots.

Open Estates and plots in Roast ›

Add or edit names: the drop-down lists

Products, buyers, suppliers, transporters, units and the app's own lists, so everyone picks the same name instead of typing it their own way. Buyers, suppliers and transporters also keep their details.

How to

  1. Open Account › Add or edit names, or pick "Edit this list…" at the bottom of any drop-down.
  2. Add a name once; it appears in every drop-down that uses that list. Edit renames it, Hide takes it off the lists, Delete removes one you added.
  3. A name typed under "Other (type it)" joins the list on its own.
  4. Tap a buyer, supplier or transporter to keep GSTIN, address, phone, bank, UPI and credit days.
  5. Inputs and tools bought: tap an item (urea, a spray, a knife) to see who sells it, which brand, pack and last price. Each purchase you record adds or updates that line, and a supplier's page lists what they sell.
  6. My business (top of Add or edit names): your own name, GSTIN, address, UPI ID and bank, used on payment requests.

Open Add or edit names in Roast ›

Map

Outlines and spots on a satellite map, with the trails and rows you have recorded.

How to

  1. Map › pick a plot › Mark: tap each corner, then Finish. Area and height are worked out.
  2. Add a spot for a store, shed, water source or gate.
  3. Trails you walk show on the map in the colour of their kind (see Trails below).
  4. Save and share: a map link, KML for Google Earth, GeoJSON, or a printed sheet.

Open Map in Roast ›

Trails

Walk something with the phone and keep its line: a plot walk, a footpath, road, drain, fence or boundary, a working route, or the rows of plants. Add stops with notes and photos on the way. Trails are kept on this phone only, not in your account, so save a backup now and then.

How to

  1. Trails › ● Start a trail. Allow location when the phone asks.
  2. Pick what the trail is (path, road, drain, fence, route…). The kind sets its colour here and on the Map; you can change it later.
  3. Tap ● Start and walk. Keep the screen on and the page open: phones stop giving the location to a web page when the screen goes off. ❚❚ Pause for a break, ● Resume to carry on.
  4. On the way: 📷 Photo here for a picture at that spot, ＋ Stop for a note (a spring, a damaged tree, a gate, a soil pit).
  5. Finish when you are done. Rename it, change the kind, add stops on the map, or edit a stop’s note and photos.
  6. Distance, time and climb show for each trail. Rough GPS fixes (worse than about 50 m) are left out.
  7. Share or save one trail: Trail pack (.zip with photos and a page that opens anywhere), GPX for hiking apps, KML for Google Earth, or GeoJSON.
  8. Back up all trails (.zip) from the Trails list, and keep the file in Drive or Files. Open a trail file brings a pack or backup back, on this phone or a new one.
  • To map plant rows, walk up one row, cross over, walk down the next and so on in one trail; then open Rows › From a trail and give the spacing.
  • GPS is best in the open and weaker under thick canopy. Stand still a few seconds at corners and row ends.
  • Clearing the browser’s site data, or uninstalling, removes trails that were never saved as a file.

Open Trails in Roast ›

Rows and plants

Each row of a plot as a line on the map, with its plants placed along it at the spacing you give, numbered and labelled (R3-12), each with its own status and note.

How to

  1. Rows › pick the plot. The first time, add one row in any of four ways:
  2. From a trail: Trails › Record, walk up the first row, turn, down the next, and so on; Stop. Then Rows › From a trail › pick it. Each straight run between the turns is offered as a row: tick the ones that are rows, give the spacing in the row, Make these rows.
  3. Walk a row: stand at the first plant, Start, walk to the last, Stop.
  4. Draw a row: tap its start and its end on the satellite map (and any bends).
  5. Copy a row alongside: once one row is right, copy it across the plot at the spacing between rows.
  6. Open a row to rename it, give a label prefix, the spacing, where the first plant stands, the variety and the year planted. Reverse direction if the numbers run the wrong way.
  7. Tap a plant on the map (zoom in close to see the numbers), or open All plants in this row, to mark it Healthy, Weak, Sick, Dead, Gap or Replanted with a note.
  8. Kind of row: main crop, intercrop, short-term crop, shade, boundary and so on. Each kind has its own colour on the map; tap a colour under Colours to change it, and add or rename kinds in Add or edit names › Row kinds. The plot outline shows dashed in the Boundary colour.
  9. Export CSV or GeoJSON, or print the map.
  • Phone GPS is good to a few metres, so a dot may sit a little off the real plant; its number along the row is what counts. Stop for a few seconds at each row end while walking.
  • If the first plant is not right at the start of the line, set "First plant from the start".

Open Rows and plants in Roast ›

Weather

Daily rain and temperature for each place with a GPS point, from free weather services, kept year after year.

How to

  1. Weather › pick a place › Get the weather. Choose how far back.
  2. Leave "keep up to date" on and the last days are added every night.
  3. Have your own rain gauge or station file? Bring it in as a file.

Open Weather in Roast ›

Field log

What went on each plot and when: nutrients, watering, plant health and work done.

How to

  1. Pick the tab: Nutrients, Watering, Plant health or Work done › ＋ New entry.
  2. Choose the place and the date, fill what you know, Save.
  3. For a disease or damage, tap 📍 Use my location under the tree so it shows on the Map.
  4. Each tab shows a summary for the year: nutrients per hectare, watering, trees lost, jobs done.

Open Field log in Roast ›

Team and wages

Workers and their details, the daily muster with a GPS check, leave, advances and the month's wages.

How to

  1. Workers › ＋ Worker: name, role, pay (by the day, month, hour or piece) and the rate. More details holds address, emergency contact, how wages are paid, skills and task.
  2. Muster each day: tap P, H, A, L or O for each worker and Save. The phone's GPS is kept with it.
  3. Hourly workers: put the hours in "Hours, overtime and notes".
  4. Month and wages: days, overtime, piece work from Jobs, advances and the net pay, ready to print.
  • A changed mark or pay rate asks for a reason and keeps the old one in the log.

Open Team and wages in Roast ›

Jobs and piece rates

Field work by place and day: who did it, how much and at what rate. Jobs done add to the month's wages.

How to

  1. ＋ New job: date, kind of work, place.
  2. Paid by quantity, days, hours or a fixed sum; the rate last used for that work fills in.
  3. Put each worker's quantity, Save. Mark it done to send it to wages.

Open Jobs and piece rates in Roast ›

Sales and money

The sales sheet, money received and money paid out, and what each buyer still owes.

How to

  1. Sale: buyer and product from the lists, quantity, rate; the amount works itself out. A lot can fill it. The buyer's GSTIN and credit days show, and the payment due date fills in.
  2. Dispatch (inside a sale): transporter, vehicle, driver phone, e-way bill, LR number, freight, dispatched and delivered dates.
  3. Open a saved sale › Ask for payment: a message with amount, due date and your bank, a UPI QR the buyer scans, sent by WhatsApp or share.
  4. Receipt: money in from a buyer. Payment: money out; a supplier with a UPI ID gets a Pay by UPI link. Under What was bought, pick the item, brand and quantity; earlier brands and prices from that supplier show as taps.
  5. Summary: payments due and late, totals for each month, what each buyer owes. Export to CSV for the accountant.

Open Sales and money in Roast ›

Land and dues

Land records, taxes and dues with the next due date, and licences with their renewal dates.

How to

  1. Add each land record: survey number, area, ownership, documents.
  2. Add dues (land tax, insurance, loan) with the next due date; Record payment when paid.
  3. Due soon lists what falls due in the next two months.

Your data

How to

  2. Open a saved file on Account to restore it on any phone.

Business, and you and your data

Business

Team and wages, field jobs, sales and money, land and dues, and the names lists behind every form.

Team and wages
Workers and their details, the daily muster with GPS, and the month's wages.Pay by the day, month, hour or piece. Details: address, emergency contact, how wages are paid, skills and task. Leave, holidays, advances and bonuses; a changed mark keeps the old one with a reason.
Field jobs and piece rates
Who did what work, how much and at what rate.Paid by quantity, days, hours or a fixed sum; the rate last used fills in. Jobs done add to the month's wages.
Sales and money
The sales sheet, money in and out, what each buyer owes, and payments due.Due dates from each buyer's credit days; dispatch with transporter, vehicle, e-way bill and freight; Ask for payment with your UPI QR, by WhatsApp or share; Pay by UPI to a supplier.
Land and dues
Land records, taxes and dues with the next due date, and licences to renew.Due soon lists what falls due in the next two months; a payment can go straight to Sales and money.
Add or edit names
The names the drop-downs offer: products, buyers, suppliers, transporters, units.Add, edit or hide names; anything typed under Other joins the list. Buyers, suppliers and transporters keep GSTIN, address, phone, bank, UPI and credit days. My business holds your own GSTIN, UPI and bank for payment requests.
Shared spaces
Brew, roast, cup or process one coffee with others and compare.The owner creates a space and invites people by email. Each person adds a copy of their own brews, roasts, cuppings or process runs, and everyone comments. The owner can also turn on a read-only public link. Needs sign-in. Open any brew, cupping, process run or roast and tap Share to a space.

You and your data

Your start page, tiles and search, and where your records live: this phone, your account, exports and backups.

Home
The front door: Find, My Now, and the four homes (Farm, Lots, Roast and cup, Business).Each home lists its pages with a count of your records. The KoffyKraft name at the top of every page comes back here.
Now: your tiles
Your own board of tiles from anywhere on the chain, land to cup.Tap Tiles to choose: plots to look at (no location, no land check, outline changed since the check), field log, weather, jobs, harvests this week, live process runs with Reading, green stock, resting roasts, last brews with Brew again, team, dues and money. Tiles with live records read this phone only; page tiles just open the page. Your order is kept; Use my activities starts again from your answers.
Find
One search for your plots, lots, roasts, brews and codes, and the sections inside them.Searches this phone, so it works with no signal. Typing soil lists each plot's soil with its last test and opens the plot at its Soil section; part of a lot code finds the run or lot. Voided records are found too, marked Voided. The Find bar sits at the top of Now.
Make it yours
Four questions: what you do, how deep you go, who uses the app, and where it opens.Your answers decide which pages and tiles come first, and which page the app opens on: Now, Home or any page you use often. A first visit always opens on Home. Nothing is hidden for good: every page stays one tap away under All. Kept on this phone and, when signed in, on your account so another phone gets them too. Change them any time in Account.
Works without an account
Everything saves on this phone. Nothing is sent unless you choose cloud sync.Pages open from the phone even without signal.
Cloud sync (optional)
Sign in with email to keep records on several devices.Choose per section: off, only what you pick, or everything.
Me: profile and activity
Everything you have recorded, as a grower, roaster and brewer, in one place.Activity totals, a 12-month chart and recent records. Producer, roaster and brewer books list every lot, roast and brew. Make a one-page profile with your own name, logo and colour, pick the records to show, and save it as PDF or publish a link. Tap the person icon at the top of any page.
Share as image or PDF
Turn a field, harvest, processing run, green lot or estate into an Instagram post, a story, or a PDF.Open a record and tap Image or PDF, or tap Select on a list to pick several. Drawn on your phone with your profile name, logo and colour, and sent through the share sheet to Instagram, WhatsApp or email. Notes and GPS location are left out unless you switch them on.
Export
CSV or JSON from Origin, Cup, Roastbook and Map.Look for Export on each page. CSV opens in Excel or Sheets.
Full backup
One file with all your KoffyKraft data, and import it back.Use it before changing phones or clearing the browser.

This guide is made from the app's own feature list, so it says what the app does today. Advice in the app is a guide, not a guarantee or a certificate. Questions: info@koffykraft.com.
